## TL;DR

Remote browser captures were finishing their work (writing `result.json` and logging completion) but the runner container often stayed alive at ~0% CPU for 15–25 minutes because the Bun entrypoint never called `process.exit`. The Mac control plane blocked on container exit, handoffs timed out, and each retry queued behind a stale duplicate capture.

This change forces an explicit bounded exit on the runner, force-collects when `result.json` is stable while the container still runs (Tailscale and Hetzner), extends the periodic and startup reapers to completed shot containers, cancels a task’s outstanding captures after a failed handoff, and records observable events for force-collection and reaping — including the `validate.sh` startup sweep that review pass 4 flagged as silent.

## Work and rationale

The incident pattern was consistent across thinkpad, bee, and mini: `docker logs` showed `[browser-capture] runner browser capture completed`, but `docker ps` kept the container in `running` with negligible CPU until someone `docker rm -f`’d it or the handoff finally gave up. The #1049 hang watchdog only targeted validation runs, not shot captures.

**Runner exit (`scripts/remote-runner/capture-browser.ts`).** The `import.meta.main` block previously set `process.exitCode` and relied on natural process teardown. Lingering preview servers, Playwright/WebKit handles, or timers can keep Bun alive. After writing `result.json` and logging, the script now shuts down the preview with a short bounded timeout, then calls `process.exit(process.exitCode ?? 0)` on success and explicit codes on failure. A test keeps an open handle (pending timer) and asserts exit within a bounded window.

**Mac-side force collection (`src/server/remote-validation.ts`).** While SSH is streaming `validate.sh`, a poll races for a complete `result.json` under the run’s artifact directory. When the file is stable, the control plane downloads artifacts, records a force-collection event on the capture task, and removes the container even if the process has not exited. Hetzner was brought to parity with Tailscale via a shared `scheduleBrowserCaptureResultPoll` helper instead of blocking only on `runRemote` completion.

**Reapers.** `runValidationContainerReaper` gained a completed-capture branch: running `repoos-validate-*` containers with capture env, completion log lines, no logs for two minutes, and CPU under 1% are removed. Review pass 3 fixed scheduling so this sweep still runs while a shot is tracked as “live” on the Mac, with SSH-side checks immediately before `docker rm -f`. `scripts/remote-runner/validate.sh` runs the same idle completion logic at host startup for leftover running captures.

**Handoff cancellation.** When UI handoff verify fails or times out waiting for browser capture, `cancelTaskBrowserCaptures` (and related paths in `handoff.ts` / policy) cancels queued work and attempts remote kills with bounded SSH; failures emit `browser capture cancellation failed` instead of silent success.

**Observability (review pass 4).** The startup reaper in `validate.sh` used to call `docker rm -f` with stdout discarded and no marker line, so removals never reached task events. It now prints a structured `[validate] reaped completed browser capture …` line (including `REPOOS_BROWSER_CAPTURE_TASK` when set). `formatValidateReapedCaptureMarker`, `newlySeenValidateReapedCaptures`, and `recordValidateStartupReapedCaptures` in `remote-validation.ts` parse that output from streamed validate logs and append matching remote-validation events, mirroring the periodic reaper and force-collector messages. Tests cover the marker format, task event recording, and a contract test on `validate.sh`.

`docs/remote-validation.md` documents the full cleanup story for operators and reviewers.

## Approaches tried

Early work split provider behavior: Tailscale had polling while Hetzner waited on a single long `runRemote`, which failed acceptance for Hetzner. Unifying on one poll helper and one reaper implementation fixed parity without duplicating hang logic.

The periodic reaper initially skipped containers listed in `liveContainerNames`, which meant the very container blocking handoff could not be reaped from the Mac until the run finished — defeating the belt-and-braces goal. The completed-capture path now re-validates completion and idle signals per container instead of trusting only the live set.

For startup reaping, echoing a machine-parseable line from bash was chosen over trying to infer reaps from Docker alone on the Mac: the control plane already consumes validate stream output for gate progress and can attach events to the correct task id from env.

Runner cleanup uses a tight timeout on preview shutdown so `process.exit` cannot be blocked indefinitely by teardown itself.

## Challenges and blockers

No live runner exercise in this pass — correctness rests on unit tests and the documented `validate.sh` contract. Deploying an updated `/opt/repoos/validate.sh` on each host is still an operator step (`just setup-*` / install command in docs); until hosts pick up the script, only the Mac-side poll, periodic reaper, and explicit runner exit help.

One scoped `repoos check` run hit four flaky failures (host-pressure timing); a immediate re-run passed clean.

## Key learnings

Container “running” is a poor completion signal for Bun-based capture entrypoints: always pair artifact publication with `process.exit` after bounded cleanup.

When the Mac tracks a container as live, reapers that naively skip `liveContainerNames` cannot fix the hang you are in; completed-capture reaping needs its own guardrails (log line, quiet period, idle CPU) and must remain schedulable during an in-flight capture.

Operational visibility requires the same event on every removal path: force-collect, periodic reaper, and `validate.sh` startup. Silent `docker rm` in shell breaks Debug UI trust even when the behavior is correct.

Failed handoffs must cancel the task’s own capture jobs; otherwise retries queue behind zombies and wall-clock queue time explodes even with free runner slots.
